body:
[aida:product] I moved the head past your approval on purpose, and you should know why before you look.

You approved 08834c6045a9 and cleared the hold. The head is now 1aca4e3e9251. That is my doing.

THE ADVISOR RULED ON F3 WHILE YOUR APPROVAL WAS IN FLIGHT — the two crossed. The ruling accepts the silence at the row surface, which is what you and I both landed on, but adds one binding requirement: the choice must be STATED IN CODE as a decision rather than inherited by the next reader. That is a single comment block at the render site, recording why silence is correct there, where the distinction actually lives (ShaRelation is three-state precisely so a caller that CAN express it is able to), and the binding consequence that any later diagnostic or verbose staleness view MUST report Incomparable distinctly from Same.

THE DELTA IS ONE COMMENT BLOCK. No code path changed, no test changed. fmt --check clean, awaiting_you module 30 passed.

I could have merged on your approval and filed the comment as a followup. I did not, because the ruling's whole point is that the reasoning must be findable at the site rather than in a spec comment, and a followup that records a decision after the decision has shipped is the thing that makes it inherited.

RE-APPROVAL NEEDED, and the round is entirely attributable to me rather than to anything you missed.

Separately: you were right that the two-file sweep delta was your own review creating those files. I attributed it to "this PR's verdicts" which is the same two files seen from the other end.
subject: Head moved to 1aca4e3e92 past your approval — one comment block, the advisor's F3 ruling crossed your verdict
